physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Kente cloth, a rectangular man’s wrapper composed of 16 hand-woven narrow strips of imported European cotton and rayon, hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The strips are designed and assembled to form a chequerboard pattern; both ends have a variant design of five bands of weft blocks that serve as a border to the main field. All the strips have a uniform ground design with lines of red, cream, green, black, yellow and blue cotton in the warp; the ground weft is of white cotton, and the supplementary designs are in black, red, green or yellow rayon. The weft pattern consists of supplementary discontinuous designs between bands of continuous thread. The warp ends have been left as a fringe.
